context.body: Now there was a long war between Saul’s house and David’s house. David grew stronger and stronger, but Saul’s house grew weaker and weaker.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: War continues as David’s house grows stronger; after conflict with Ishbosheth, Abner negotiates, Michal is returned, and elders hear his proposal.
observations.label: Abner turns toward covenant with David: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, Abner, Ishbosheth, Michal, elders, and Benjamin, Hebron, Mahanaim, and Israel’s tribal assemblies, growing, accusing, negotiating, requiring a wife’s return, speaking to elders, feasting, and sending away in peace visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Abner turns toward covenant with David: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: David, Abner, Ishbosheth, Michal, elders, and Benjamin · Hebron, Mahanaim, and Israel’s tribal assemblies · growing, accusing, negotiating, requiring a wife’s return, speaking to elders, feasting, and sending away in peace · a transfer of allegiance approaches through disputed household and political claims
observations.label: Relationships named in 2 Samuel 3:1–21

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 3:1–21 as its own judah, conflict, and unification David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places a transfer of allegiance approaches through disputed household and political claims inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: Abner turns toward covenant with David
